text:
lina: heads up - after last night's drive-firmware rollout in eu-west2 we started seeing nodes remount read-only and some NVMe metadata CRC errors. GPUs failing to attach for a subset of low-latency queues.

rick: saw that. most failures are `EXT4-fs error (device nvme0n1p3): ext4_journal_check_start`. jobs queueing back up.

noa: telemetry: sudden spike in metadata write ops around 02:14 UTC, correlates with firmware push window. affected cohort: eu-west2-hotstripe-3.

capacity: how many GPUs impacted? need estimate for scheduled jobs.

lina: ~18 GPUs across 12 hosts showing attach hiccups, ~65 pending attach attempts in last 30m. some hosts auto-evicted earlier when FS remounted ro.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-042, severity P1 (provisioning blocked). paging eng-oncall.

rick: quick mitigation suggestions? rollback firmware or force failover? rollback might be noisy.

noa: can we remount rw and run `fsck -y`? risk of hitting further IO errors while fixing.

lina: I propose two-track: (A) immediate live failover of critical GPU queues to eu-west2-cold (spin up reserved burst), (B) isolate and patch small batch of hosts with targeted rollback + fsck. do both in parallel.

capacity: cost check: spinning reserved burst for critical queues ~ $2k/hr. doing full rollback + reboots one-off labor ~ $6k. if we only do hot queue failover for 3 hours cost ~= $6k total.

rick: prefer minimal blast radius: failover + isolate 4 worst hosts for rollback. keep janitor off them.

storage-bot: SMART alert: nvme cohort eu-west2-hotstripe-3 shows increased Reallocated_Sector_Ct and metadata CRC errors. predictive: firmware write path unstable. recommend immediate firmware holdback.

noa: ops playbook step to holdback firmware is `infra/firmware/holdback.sh --region eu-west2 --cohort hotstripe-3`. also flag the canary pool.

lina: executing holdback now.

ops-bot: holdback script queued by lina: infra/firmware/holdback.sh --region eu-west2 --cohort hotstripe-3 (in progress).

capacity: spinning 20 cold GPUs now. ETA ~4m. will route critical queue to those.

rick: once cold GPUs up, we should drain failing nodes (graceful) and run `e2fsck -f -y` before re-enabling. sample commands:```bash
ssh ops@gnode-503 sudo umount /scratch || true
sudo e2fsck -f -y /dev/nvme0n1p3
sudo mount /scratch
```

noa: small warning: e2fsck may take long on 4TB scratch volumes. prefer run on isolated hosts only.

lina: agreed. we'll rotate through 3 hosts at a time. monitor attach latencies.

ops-bot: cold GPUs ready: 20 GPUs allocated in eu-west2-cold. routing rule applied for critical-llq.

rick: attach backlog dropping. good sign. will start drains in batches.

lina: ACTIONS: (1) holdback firmware (done), (2) allocate cold GPUs (done), (3) drain+fsck 3 hosts at a time, (4) update cost ticket with burst estimate.

capacity: logging cost ticket: ticket#3421. estimate preliminary ~ $6k for 3h of reserved burst + ops time.

noa: suggest we add a telemetry regression alert: `metadata_crc_errors > 5 && remount_ro_count > 0` to trigger auto-holdback next time.

lina: please add. also schedule a postmortem to decide whether to revert firmware across all regions or only rework the write-path patch.

storage-bot: post-drain e2fsck results: gnode-503: 12 corrupted inodes repaired, mount successful. gnode-507: clean. full report in attached log link.

rick: rolling drains proceeding. GPUs re-attaching. pending queue down to 8.

lina: thanks team. labeling incident: remediation-in-progress. will update with final cost and retro time. :white_check_mark:
